catalog_citation: Ebarb, Kristopher J. 2014. Tone and Variation in Idakho and Other Luhya Varieties. PhD dissertation, Indiana University, Bloomington. xii+538 pp. (UMI 3640905; PQDT Open, 'published as open access'). Corroborating first-hand for Tiriki: Paster, Mary & Yuni Kim. 2011. Downstep in Tiriki. Linguistic Discovery 9(1): 71-104, sec. 3.1 p. 78.
catalog_locator: Ebarb 2014, sec. 1.1 p. 6 and sec. 1.5 p. 37 (whole work consulted: 'stress' occurs only in two reference titles, pp. 533-534)
catalog_quote: The tone bearing unit in Idakho is the mora. At surface representation, the mora may bear either a high tone (henceforth, H) or a low tone (henceforth L); at underlying and intermediate representations, moras may also be unspecified for tone. ... "falling tone" is not a phonological category in Idakho ... [p. 6] ... Idakho is a conservative variety of Luhya, contrasting between underlyingly /H/ and /Ø/ classes of verbal roots. The present work identifies 8 distinct patterns ... distinguished by the number and position of melodic Hs within the macrostem, the tonal properties of verbal affixes, and how melodic Hs interact with the verb’s position in the phrase. [p. 37]
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work is listed, so the two-work spot-check was applied to that work plus the prior-pass files already stored under this glottocode. a full-text search for stress/accent all 14 saved files for stress|penult(imate)|accent|accentuat|prominence: Nandama 2022 (UoN MA, Lwisukha noun tone) p. 1 says a linguist 'can classify dialects by investigating tone and stress' (a general typological remark) and p. 28 sec. 2.1 lists 'tone, intonation, stress, vowel length and pitch' as suprasegments then studies tone only; its syllable section (ch. 2) quotes Kenstowicz on the nucleus as 'tone or stress bearing unit' (general). Paster & Kim 2011, Nandama & Oduor 2020/2022: 'penultimate' occurs only in…

sources.citation: Nandama, Sussy K. 2022. A Study of the Tone System of Lwisukha Nouns. MA thesis, University of Nairobi (hdl 11295/162079), xx+352 pp.
sources.note: Ch.2 (p.28) lists 'tone, intonation, stress, vowel length and pitch among others' as Lwisukha suprasegments but states only tone is treated; p.1 mentions 'tone and stress' as possible dialect-classification criteria. No statement of where stress falls. Body: Lwisukha has H, L, downstepped H and toneless syllables; 39 noun tone patterns in isolation; HTA and H-tone-insertion rules.

Sec.3.1 'Basics of Tiriki tonology' (p.78): TBU is the mora; underlying three-way contrast H / toneless / L reducing to surface H vs L (+downstepped H); Meeussen's Rule, H Tone Anticipation, default L insertion. sources.note: 'an original description and analysis of processes in the morphophonology of several Luyia languages of western Kenya, focusing on the differential behaviour of long vowels.. We also discuss tonal patterns which differ from one another in their sensitivity to vowel length differences. We show that some tonal rules operate solely in terms of moras, while others require reference to whole syllables, irrespective of whether the syllable has a long or short vowel. Others still are sensitive to vowel length differences in some syllables but not others.' The Crossref-deposited reference list cites…
